title: A counit triangle from essential image and orthogonality
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be pretriangulated [def-weil-triangulated-category], $\mathcal D$ a category, and $F:\mathcal D\rightleftarrows\mathcal C:G$ an adjunction with $F$ fully faithful. Let $X\to Y\xrightarrow v Z\to X[1]$ be distinguished, with $X$ in the essential image of $F$, and suppose $\operatorname{Hom}((FM)[n],Z)$ is a subsingleton for every $M\in\mathcal D$ and every $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then the counit $FGY\to Y$ and $v$ extend to a distinguished triangle $FGY\to Y\to Z\to(FGY)[1]$.

proof.text: Orthogonality for shift zero makes the counit have zero composite to Z. Exactness of Hom into the given triangle factors the counit as b followed by X to Y.

Composition with X to Y is bijective on maps from FM: surjectivity uses zero-shift orthogonality and Hom exactness; injectivity uses shift-one orthogonality and Hom exactness after shifting. Composition with the counit is also bijective there, by full faithfulness and the adjunction Hom equivalence.

Consequently composition with b is bijective on maps from FM. Since both ends of b are in the essential image of F, take preimages of their identity maps to construct a two-sided inverse for b. Transport the given distinguished triangle through b. Its boundary is the old boundary followed by b inverse shifted by one.
